title: How to Train an AI to Create Your Own Pixel Art
author: YungMixtape2004

comments.author: RandomFlareA
comments.body:
None of the pixels in these are the same size... not pixel art.

This is just normal ai training

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: I haven't watched yet but all you have to do is use the mosaic tool in Photoshop to change that. Takes about 5 seconds, although sometimes boarders need to be fixed.

replies.author: RandomFlareA
replies.body: I guess but then there is still a bunch of work ti clean it up and id need to hire an artist :(

replies.author: speederaser
replies.body:
As someone who is in the process of publishing a pixel art AI game, that workflow isn't all that bad actually. It's taken my shitty pixel art to passable. Before I would spend hours drawing one animation. Now I just spend a few minutes cleaning up an AI image.


I admit that the pixel art Loras aren't that much better than regular 2D art plus Photoshop. They both need Photoshop, but the pixel art Loras gets you closer to the shading one would expect for clicking the pixelate button on Photoshop.

replies.author: DangerousImplication
replies.body: Can you elaborate on how mosaic tool can be used? I’m actually looking to generate low res AI pixel art with perfectly sized pixels and coherent overall look.

replies.author: crumbaker
replies.body: filter/pixelate/mosaic then whatever cell size looks good to you
